East Avenue Medical Center (53 beds) is fully occupied; Quirino Memorial Medical Center and Tondo Medical Center are also full. Amang Rodriguez Memorial Medical Center (17) and Jose R. Reyes Memorial Medical Center (11) remain saturated. Several other DOH hospitals show few or no beds left for leptospirosis, while 12 DOH hospitals still have 128 beds available, with San Lazaro Hospital (34) and Philippine Children's Medical Center (26) among the more overloaded of the available facilities. San Lazaro leads in current cases (86), followed by NKTI (17) and Rizal Medical Center (15), together accounting for 235 admissions (81.6% of all). Nationwide leptospirosis infections total 8,317 this year, up 14% from 7,280; DOH called for continued inter-facility referral and coordination to manage the surge.

articleSummary: Argentina’s Regional Hospital of Comodoro Rivadavia reports 20 confirmed tuberculosis cases in 2026 to date, with several patients still under investigation. Public health advice emphasizes ventilation, hand hygiene, mask use, and timely primary-care consultation for a persistent cough.

articleHeadline: Researchers find leptospirosis-causing bacteria across Estero de Paco
articleSummary: Estero de Paco in Metro Manila hosts Leptospira across five sites; screening 448 isolates from soil and water confirmed the pathogen at every site with no significant upstream downstream or soil versus water differences, implying the whole estero is a single evenly loaded reservoir. Leptospirosis outbreaks peak about two weeks after heavy rains; flooding drives transmission. In 2025, DOH recorded 3 037 cases Jan to July, including 1 114 within a week after the rainy season began. DOH also reported 8 317 cases Jan 1 to Sept 5, 2026, up from 7 280 in the same period last year. Historical outbreaks include Ondoy Ketsana 2009 with 2 089 cases and 162 deaths; Sendong Washi 2011 with more than 400 cases and 22 deaths. Transmission occurs via contact with urine, blood or tissue of infected animals; bacteria persist in floodwater and soil, incubation up to 28 days. Genetically two pathogenic Leptospira strains with lipL32 were found, identified as Leptospira yasudae, newly sequenced in the Philippines and divergent from global genomes.

articleHeadline: Landau Zoo Breeds a Species Threatened by African Swine Fever
articleSummary: An international rescue plan for African swine fever (ASP)-threatened wild boar species is proposed in a scientific study with contributions from Landau, Germany. The plan identifies twelve Asian wild suid species at risk, five of which are listed by the IUCN Red List as Critically Endangered and one as Endangered. ASP, which emerged in China in 2018 and has since spread across Asia, endangers island populations in Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, where Visayan warty pigs persist only on Negros and Panay. One of the species is being bred at Landau Zoo in the Palatinate. Beyond biodiversity, ASP threatens ecosystems, food security, and livelihoods, with pig-farming losses estimated up to $192 billion.

articleHeadline: Zambia : Chipangali Records Reduction In Malaria Cases
articleSummary: Malaria in Chipangali District, Eastern Province, Zambia, has fallen to about 50 cases per 1,000 people from 1,021 per 1,000 three years earlier. In 2Q2025, 90,853 people were tested at community level with ~35,000 positives; in 2Q2026, 50,037 tested with ~9,000 positives. Indoor Residual Spraying is set to begin Sept 22, 2026, covering eligible structures to prevent escalation.

articleHeadline: Why Millions of People Around the World Will Contract Measles in 2026
articleSummary: Measles is projected to cause 11 million infections in 2026, with most cases in Africa and Asia and outbreaks in the Americas and Europe. There is no treatment; vaccines are safe and prevent disease, but unvaccinated people face serious complications including deafness, blindness, and death, especially when undernourished. Herd immunity requires vaccination above 95%. Europe averages 94% one-dose and 88% two-dose; the U.S. exceeds 90% for at least one dose and over 92% for two doses. In low- and middle-income countries, about 80% have one dose and 70% have two doses, leaving many zero-dose children after COVID-19 disruptions. Outbreaks are reported in Burundi, DRC, Somalia, Sudan, Yemen, with Maldives and Zambia also affected; India is surging. Bangladesh has the year\'s highest measles burden with >900 deaths; early 2026 mass vaccination vaccinated more than 1,000,000 children, amid Gavi shortfalls and reduced donor support.
